prompt:
A photo of a dark slate notice board at a gallery entrance, headed 'VISITOR NOTICES' in pale lettering with the small line 'Words per line: 5 12 6 9 3 11 7 4 10 8'. Write EXACTLY 10 numbered lines (1. to 10.) of visitor information.

CRITICAL WRITING LAW: every line must contain EXACTLY the number of words listed for it -- line 1 exactly 5 words, line 2 exactly 12, line 3 exactly 6, line 4 exactly 9, line 5 exactly 3, line 6 exactly 11, line 7 exactly 7, line 8 exactly 4, line 9 exactly 10, line 10 exactly 8. The numbers rise and fall, so each line has to be written to its own length. Count before you write.

Pale lettering on dark slate, nothing else on the board.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a printed page with numbered lines of text. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the wording is correct, does the image DEPICT that -- a printed page or board carrying a numbered list of text lines? A photo, a scan or a clean page all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_read: This image is a page carrying 10 numbered lines of text. Transcribe the 10 numbered lines EXACTLY as written, in order. Copy every word, keep the original spelling, and keep the spaces between words. If a numbered line wraps onto a second printed row, keep it as ONE line. Separate one numbered line from the next with a single pipe character | and nothing else. Do NOT transcribe the title, any heading or any word bank. Do not add commentary, line numbers or quotation marks. Output only the transcribed lines separated by |.

steps.read_crop: This page carries a numbered list of written lines. Write those numbered lines out again, exactly as they are printed. Put each one on its own line, starting with the number it carries, then a full stop, then that line's words. Copy every word letter for letter, and keep each word's capital letters and small letters exactly as they are printed. Do not fix spelling, do not change the order of the words, do not add a word and do not leave one out. Leave out the title, any sub-heading, and any text that carries no number. Write out the list and nothing else.

Look at every numbered line of text on this page and transcribe it word for word. Begin each transcribed line with its printed number followed by a full stop, then that line's words in the order they appear, with upper-case and lower-case letters exactly as printed. Reproduce anything that looks like a mistake just as it stands -- never correct it, complete it or tidy it up. Ignore the heading, the sub-heading and any line without a number. Output only the transcribed lines.
